description: The plot illustrates the performance of three methods—20NG, a gray-shaded method (likely a baseline or control, though unlabeled in the legend), and NIPS—measured by Normalized Pointwise Mutual Information (NPMI) as a function of the “weight of negative sampling,” which ranges from 0.5 to 3.0 on a linear x-axis. The y-axis, labeled “NPMI,” spans from 0.18 to 0.42, with a break near 0.22 indicating a discontinuity in scale. The black line with square markers (20NG) starts at approximately NPMI = 0.37 at weight 0.5, rises slightly to 0.38 at weight 1.0, dips to 0.37 at weight 2.0, and ends at 0.38 at weight 3.0, showing minor fluctuation. The red line with circular markers (gray-shaded method) begins at NPMI ≈ 0.195 at weight 0.5, dips to 0.19 at weight 1.0, peaks at 0.20 at weight 1.5, drops back to 0.195 at weight 2.0, and remains flat at 0.195 through weight 3.0. The blue line with triangular markers (NIPS) starts at NPMI ≈ 0.40 at weight 0.5, rises to 0.41 at weight 1.0, plateaus until weight 1.5, then declines gradually to 0.405 at weight 2.0 and 0.40 at weight 3.0. Overall, NIPS consistently outperforms the other two methods across all weights, while the gray-shaded method shows the lowest NPMI values.
